sections.title: Defining Perimeter
sections.content:
According to the source, a perimeter is defined as "the space inside a shape" (Section 1). 

Note: There appears to be a conceptual inconsistency in the source text. Typically, in geometry, 'perimeter' refers to the distance around the outside of a shape, while 'area' refers to the space inside. Because the source explicitly defines perimeter as "the space inside," this lesson follows that specific provided definition.

sections.title: Recorded Example
sections.content: The source provides a specific example of a rectangular garden (Section 1). This garden has sides measuring 5 m and 8 m. The perimeter for this specific garden is recorded as 26 m.

lesson.title: Understanding Garden Boundaries

sections.title: What is a Perimeter?
sections.content: A perimeter is defined as the total distance around the outside of a shape (Source: Section 1). In practical terms, if you were to walk along the very edge of a garden until you returned to your starting point, the total length of that path would be the perimeter.

sections.title: Example Calculation
sections.content: To understand how this works with a specific shape, consider a rectangular garden. According to the source, a rectangle with sides measuring 5 m and 8 m has a perimeter of 26 m (Source: Section 1). This total is calculated by adding all four sides together: 5 m + 8 m + 5 m + 8 m = 26 m.
